metadata.title: Bank Book / Cash Book View & Running Balances

story.iWant: to view cash/bank books with running balances and drill-down capabilities
story.soThat: I can analyze movements and verify balances accurately

tasks.task: Backend – Async Export for Large Datasets (AC: #5)

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Per-account view: filters by date/type/reference; columns show opening balance, inflow, outflow, closing; running balance after each TX with signed values.
Drill into any row to voucher detail with attachments; show posting user and timestamps; highlight negative balances with color and tooltip.
Multi-account view yields aggregated totals; toggle grouping by account; quick switcher between bank/cash; remembers last view per user.
Export to Excel/PDF; include company branding/logo, filter snapshot, timestamp, generated-by; file footer includes document hash.
Pagination or virtual list for >5k rows; download full dataset asynchronously with notification when ready; rate-limited to prevent abuse.
RBAC enforced for all queries/exports; attempts to export outside role scope fail and are audit-logged.
Performance: initial load ≤2s for typical month (≤5k TX) with indexed queries; slow queries logged.
All views/exports logged in audit with filters, user, IP, hash of snapshot data.

constraints.constraint: Follow existing service layer patterns from PaymentServiceImpl and ReceiptServiceImpl
Use CompanyContext for multi-tenant company scoping in all queries
Apply @PreAuthorize annotations for RBAC enforcement at controller level
Use standard response wrapper { data, meta, error } for all API responses
Implement audit logging for all view and export operations
Use TanStack Table with server-side pagination for large datasets
Follow i18n translation pattern: add keys to vi/en common.json, use useTranslation hook
Use localStorage for persisting user's last view preferences per company
Backend tests use JUnit 5 + TestContainers for integration tests
Frontend tests use Vitest + Testing Library + jsdom
Initial load target ≤2s for typical month (≤5k transactions)
Add query latency telemetry logging for performance monitoring
All exports must include document hash (SHA256) for integrity verification
Export throttling to prevent bulk data extraction abuse

interface.name: GET /api/v1/cash-book/:bankAccountId
interface.signature: Query: dateFrom, dateTo, type=receipt|payment|all, reference, page, size; Response: { data: { account, openingBalance, transactions[], closingBalance, totalInflow, totalOutflow }, meta }

interface.name: GET /api/v1/cash-book/:bankAccountId/transactions/:voucherId
interface.signature: Response: { data: VoucherDetailDTO with lines and attachments }

interface.name: GET /api/v1/cash-book/summary
interface.signature: Query: dateFrom, dateTo, accountIds; Response: { data: { accounts[], grandTotals } }

interface.name: GET /api/v1/cash-book/:bankAccountId/export
interface.signature: Query: format=EXCEL|PDF, dateFrom, dateTo; Response: Binary file with branding, hash

interface.name: CashBookService
interface.signature: getCashBook(bankAccountId, filters, pageable), getCashBookSummary(accountIds, dateRange), getVoucherDetail(voucherId)

tests.standards: Backend uses JUnit 5 with Spring Boot Test for unit tests and TestContainers for PostgreSQL integration tests. Frontend uses Vitest with Testing Library and jsdom for component tests. E2E tests use Playwright for workflow verification. All tests must cover company scoping and RBAC enforcement. Performance tests should verify query latency meets ≤2s target for typical datasets.
